native_result.query: Between which two races is the factor of BA degree completion -0.9568 when compared to the other?
native_result.HypoA: There is a racial differential in BA degree completion rates between Black and White students with a factor of -0.9568.
native_result.HypoB: The factor -0.9568 for BA degree completion arises when Black respondents are compared with White respondents (White as reference): in the logit model BA ~ SAMPLE_RACE * SES the Black main effect is -0.9568 (SE 0.2154, p = 8.8e-06), i.e. at SES = 0 Black respondents have exp(-0.9568) = 0.384 times the odds of completing a BA that White respondents have (about 62% lower odds). In the transparent race-only logit the Black-vs-White log-odds ratio is -1.0057 (OR 0.366, 95% CI 0.245-0.546, p = 8.4e-07) and the Hispanic-vs-White one is -0.9241 (OR 0.397, 95% CI 0.247-0.639, p = 1.4e-04), with crude BA completion shares of 1.33% (Black), 1.44% (Hispanic) and 3.54% (White); the Black-White pair is the answer under every specification checked (crude, race+SES, race*SES contrasts at SES quartiles and ATC, Firth/ridge refits), and among 252 race terms scanned across 42 formulas and 3 reference categories only the Black-vs-White term in the race x SES model rounds to -0.9568, so the Hispanic-White reading is rejected.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Inspection of data/nls_ses_processed.csv (8773 rows, 0 missing, exact column names, BA DEGREE COMPLETED stored as True/False mapped to 1/0). 2) Descriptives: BA shares by race and pairwise crude odds ratios with Woolf CIs and chi-square tests. 3) Primary specification logit(BA ~ SAMPLE_RACE) with dummy coding and White as reference: coefficients, SE, z, p, 95% CI and odds ratios (section B). 4) Target-reproducing specification logit(BA ~ SAMPLE_RACE * SES) with White as reference, where the Black main effect is -0.956778 -> -0.9568 at 4 dp, reported explicitly as the Black-vs-White log-odds ratio AT SES = 0 (SES is an approximately standardized composite: mean -0.0090, sd 0.7424, range -2.45..2.72), not the average effect (section C). 5) Robustness: linear-combination (delta-method) contrasts at SES quartiles 0.25/0.50/0.75, ATC-style contrast at the Black group's mean SES plus a probability-scale ATC from 2000 parametric-bootstrap draws, and AIC/BIC/LR comparison of race-only, race+SES and race*SES (section D). 6) Rare-event diagnostics: events-per-parameter, convergence status/iterations, Firth penalized-likelihood and ridge refits (section E). 7) Uniqueness grid over 42 formulas x 3 reference categories (all covariate subsets of SES, ABILITY, PERCENTILE, FAMILY SIZE, sex plus race-by-covariate interactions) to identify which race term equals -0.9568 and to test the Hispanic-White alternative (section F). Environment: python 3.12.14, pandas 3.0.2, numpy 2.4.4, statsmodels 0.14.6; Newton solver, tol 1e-12, seed 20261025 for the bootstrap.
